activities.anchor: The discipline's first argument defines its poles
activities.caption: file each technique by the camp that trusts it
activities.name: ftcPolesBuckets

config.prompt: Formalism or realism — file each claim and technique:

items.label: shot A of a face plus shot B of a plate of soup
Italian neorealism's non-professional actors in real streets

config.why: Neither camp was naive: Bazin believed ideology lives in technique, and Eisenstein believed reality's meaning needed construction — every style is an argument about the real.

activities.caption: pair each mode with its exemplar
activities.name: ftcModesMatch

config.prompt: Nichols' six modes, six exemplars — pair them:

pairs.right: voice-of-god narration — the 1930s March of Time tradition
direct cinema — the Maysles brothers, Wiseman
the filmmaker enters the frame — Michael Moore's interviews
the film shows its own making — Man with a Movie Camera's cameraman
the filmmaker's own experience as evidence — personal documentary

config.why: Each mode is a different answer to the same ethics: who speaks, and who is spoken for.

activities.caption: true or false — the objectivity audit
activities.name: ftcDocJudge

statements.s: Every documentary is a set of choices — what to shoot, whom to interview, what to leave on the cutting-room floor.
statements.why: Those choices are the authorship — even before a single cut is made.

statements.s: The honest claim a documentary can make is 'this is reality.'
statements.why: The honest claim is 'this is a faithful argument about reality' — and the critic audits the argument.

statements.s: 'Does the music editorialise?' is a fair question to ask of a documentary's edit.
statements.why: Whose voices are absent, which footage does the edit recontextualise — documentary criticism is applied film theory.

statements.s: Documentary criticism's stakes are lower than fiction criticism's because nothing is invented.
statements.why: The stakes are reputations, policies and justice — not just endings.

activities.anchor: The debates stay live because the theory invites both use and abuse
activities.caption: the lens and its corrections — drag between them
activities.name: ftcGazeCompare

config.prompt: The gaze: 1975 and after — drag the divider:

before.label: the 1970s lens
before.text: Apparatus theory and Mulvey: darkened room, fixed seat, projected image — ideology built into the seat; classical Hollywood organises looking around the male gaze, women displayed as spectacle, men driving the action.

after.label: the corrections
after.text: bell hooks' oppositional gaze and queer spectatorship: Mulvey's spectator was itself unmarked — male, white, straight by default. And over-application flattens films whose women are simultaneously objects and the films' intelligences.

config.why: The mature position: the gaze is a hypothesis about structure, not a verdict about audiences — apply it with evidence about how this film actually arranges looking.

config.prompt: Filmmakers' manifestos across the century — put them in chronological order:
items: Truffaut's Cahiers polemic — 'a certain tendency in French cinema'
config.why: From the machine-eye to the vow of chastity: the loop the film ladder keeps drawing closes here — today's grammar lesson is yesterday's theory essay.

activities.anchor: Genre theory treats film categories as
activities.caption: the western's contract — trace each choice
activities.name: ftcGenreBranch

config.root: You are developing a western. The genre's contract promises landscape, violence with meaning and the frontier's moral problem.

start.text: What do you do with the contract?

choices.label: Honour every clause
choices.feedback: Genre as ritual — audiences renewing shared values.

choices.label: Break the myth on purpose
choices.feedback: Unforgiven's move — and it only reads if the audience knows the contract.

choices.label: Keep the hats and horses, drop the moral geometry

ritual.text: The contract honoured: expectations renewed rather than spent. Safe at the box office — and invisible to genre-literate critics.

subversion.text: Unforgiven (1992) spends the western's accumulated expectations to argue against the myth the genre built — knowing the contract is prerequisite to reading the violation.

syntax.text: Semantics kept, syntax changed: that is how Star Wars can be a western wearing spacecraft — hats and horses are the surface, the civilisation/wilderness opposition is the syntax.

config.why: Genres are negotiated contracts that evolve by repetition and variation — the studio markets the label; the audience and the film keep renegotiating what it means.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the critic's working rules
activities.name: ftcCriticismCloze

config.text: The craft rules, learnt from the masters: %%0%% before you judge — quote the frame, since mise-en-scène analysis is the critic's evidence kit; take the film's own %%1%% seriously — a slow film is not boring for being slow; and argue from the %%2%% — every aesthetic claim points at something on screen, so the review is falsifiable in principle.
config.hint: The verdict becomes someone's syllabus — Hitchcock's elevation from entertainer to auteur was done in print.

activities.name: ftcPostTheoryBuckets

items.label: apparatus theory's darkened room and fixed seat
cognitivism — how viewers actually construct stories
